headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure and capacity onto large energy users, including data centers, to reduce the financial burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia moves to shift more power costs from families to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are shifting more grid infrastructure costs onto data centers and other large-load customers to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers. This move is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars by ensuring data centers pay the full cost of the transmission infrastructure their developments require.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption and provide better information for water resource management.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use data facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: What does Data center site assessment and sound profile for high energy use facilities (HB153) do?
news_summary: This bill requires Virginia local governments to review potential impacts before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more of electricity. Applicants must submit a site assessment studying noise and effects on nearby homes and schools within 500 feet, and localities can request reviews on water, farmland, parks, historic sites, and forests.
